newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal firms late on soy rally, oil lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal firms late on soy rally, oil lower.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended higher on Thursday, in line with gains in soybeans, as cold temperatures descended upon the central United States and increased livestock feed demand, traders said.
Soyoil futures closed lower on commercial selling tied to talk of heavy deliveries posted against the January.
The January/March soymeal spread widened further, in part due to short covering ahead of the expiry of the January contract next Wednesday.
Traders also noted demand for livestock feed increased and transportation problems worsened as the weather deteriorated.
"It's cold out there and it's getting colder," one trader said. "The rivers are freezing, the (railroad) tracks are running slowly and diesel trucks won't start."
The Jan/March spread closed at $6.80, premium January.
Soyoil was under pressure from another day of heavy deliveries and expectations for more. There were 1,282 lots of soyoil posted Thursday for delivery against the January.
Traders said Term Commodities sold at least 400 lots March soyoil which contributed to the declines. Produce Grain reportedly sold 300 lots July soyoil.
ADM, Cargill Inc, Central Soya and Continental Grain were all said to be buyers of soymeal. Refco Inc and Merrill Lynch were sellers of the March, traders said.
Soymeal closed $1.50 to $0.50 per ton higher with January up $1.30 at $242.10. Soyoil ended 0.15 to 0.22 cent per lb lower with January down 0.18 at 24.27.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 19,000 lots, against Wednesday's actual volume of 25,543. Soyoil volume was estimated at 18,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 21,906 lots.
